attempts.reason_tested: already published in CB145 (VWF or ADAMTS13 against outcome)
attempts.method: Read /core/articles/CB145_2026_thromboinflammation-virulent-babesiosis.md and searched /core/data/markdown/CB145.md for vWF, von Willebrand, ADAMTS, factor VIII and the measured-variable lists.
attempts.result: CB145 (B. rossi, Onderstepoort, 97 infected with 12 non-survivors, 15 controls; 10.3389/fvets.2026.1712262) measured PT, aPTT, FII, FVII, FX, FXI activities, fibrinogen, D-dimer, antithrombin, plasminogen, alpha-2-antiplasmin, TEG, CRP, SAA. FVII, FX and antithrombin were lower in non-survivors. vWF appears in the introduction and discussion as background only; no VWF antigen, VWF activity, multimers, FVIII or ADAMTS13 was measured, and the authors name the missing endothelial assessment as a limitation. So CB145 does not close this gap.

attempts.reason_tested: already published elsewhere in canine babesiosis
attempts.method: grep for willebrand|vWF|ADAMTS across /core/articles/CB*.md and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md (hits: CB028, CB145, CB278, CB385, CB446, CB493); read each context; CB385 checked in /core/search/extraction_records.jsonl. PubMed query (dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (babesia OR babesiosis) AND ("von Willebrand" OR vWF OR ADAMTS13 OR "factor VIII"), 2026-11-12.
attempts.result: PubMed gave 3 records; only 10.1111/jvim.12146 (CB446) measures VWF in babesiosis: 12 naturally infected dogs before treatment vs 10 healthy, vWF activity lower, FVIII unchanged, no severity or outcome split. The others are a Rangelia vitalii immunohistochemistry paper (10.1016/j.vetpar.2005.07.011) and a von Willebrand disease case report (10.2460/javma.2003.222.959). CB028 and CB493 are reviews restating CB446. CB385 (Kules et al. 2010, same Zagreb group, title only, scope_label unverifiable) is probably the same dogs as CB446. CB278, a review (10.56093/ijvasr.v53i1.152192), cites a B. gibsoni report of raised vWF and propeptide falling after therapy: a pre/post-treatment contrast, not severity, and that primary article is not in PubMed or the CB set. ADAMTS13 has never been measured in canine babesiosis. No canine severity or outcome contrast exists.

attempts.reason_tested: human severity evidence weak or unverified
attempts.method: Resolved the grid DOIs in PubMed and read the abstracts: 10.1371/journal.ppat.1000349 (HU009), 10.1186/s12936-019-3040-3; plus 10.1097/CCM.0000000000004469 found by search.
attempts.result: Direction confirmed but the cohorts are small. Ghana, 20 severe and 13 cerebral malaria (10.1371/journal.ppat.1000349): VWF collagen binding 7.0-7.6 vs 1.9 IU/mL, ultra-large multimers present, ADAMTS13 activity about 55% of normal, p < 0.005. Post-mortem lungs in malaria-associated ARDS (10.1186/s12936-019-3040-3): intravascular VWF raised, endothelial lining VWF reduced. Paediatric severe malaria, n = 464 (10.1097/CCM.0000000000004469): VWF among the endothelial markers raised with severity and AKI. The two 2025-2026 DOIs in the grid row were not verified here. Several cohorts agree on direction, but the central VWF/ADAMTS13 ratio evidence rests mainly on one small Ghanaian cohort.

attempts.reason_tested: direction differs between species (the canine result goes the other way)
attempts.method: Compared CB446 with the human cohorts above.
attempts.result: In the one canine measurement vWF activity was LOWER than in healthy dogs (10.1111/jvim.12146), where human malaria shows higher VWF antigen and activity. This does not reject a severity gap, because CB446 has no severity contrast and measured activity (not antigen or multimers) in B. canis, a less virulent species; the lung study shows that endothelial vWF can fall while circulating vWF rises. It does weaken the assumed direction of transfer: a canine study must measure VWF:Ag, VWF activity and ADAMTS13 together and cannot assume the human sign.

Both assays exist. A human ADAMTS13 activity ELISA was validated for dog plasma (intra-assay CV 3.0-12.4%, lower in bacteraemic dogs, p = 0.0025; 10.1177/1040638714523609), and a reference interval of > 0.45 IU/mL was set in 40 healthy dogs with a commercial kit (10.1111/vcp.70052). Canine VWF:Ag ELISAs are routine in von Willebrand disease testing, although the grid's validation citation has no DOI. Haemolysed and icteric babesiosis samples may interfere; not tested here.

attempts.method: grep GN=VWF and GN=ADAMTS13 in /core/data/raw/DS07/B_Proteins.txt; grep of /experiments/shared/tidy/*.json; SV-06a grid columns.
attempts.result: Neither protein is in DS07 and neither appears in any tidy feature file. DS06 holds VWF and ADAMTS13 RNA in 5 experimental Beagles with no severity contrast, and ADAMTS13 is made in the liver while VWF is stored in endothelium and platelets, so blood RNA is a poor proxy. A test needs stored citrated plasma: CH03 (CB145, 97 dogs, 12 deaths) is the best match because the rest of the coagulation panel is already measured there.

verdict_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured VWF or ADAMTS13 against severity or outcome, and CB145, the obvious threat, measured factor activities but not VWF or ADAMTS13. Validated canine assays exist for both. The lead is weakened because the human VWF/ADAMTS13 ratio evidence rests largely on one small cohort and because the single canine measurement (CB446) found vWF activity lower, not higher, than in controls, so the direction of transfer cannot be assumed.

human_counterpart.claim: Severe and cerebral falciparum malaria: raised VWF antigen and collagen binding, ultra-large multimers, ADAMTS13 activity about 55% of normal
Malaria-associated ARDS: intravascular VWF raised with loss of endothelial-lining VWF (Weibel-Palade release)
Paediatric severe malaria: VWF among endothelial markers raised with severity and acute kidney injury
Canine babesiosis (B. canis) vs healthy dogs: vWF activity LOWER, FVIII unchanged, no severity split

canine_parallel_already_made: partly: CB446 measured vWF activity against healthy controls only (and CB278, CB028, CB493 restate it); no CB article measures ADAMTS13 or any VWF variable against severity or outcome, CB145 included
